newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fernz sees profit hike in 1998 after 1997 gains.
newsitem.headline: Fernz sees profit hike in 1998 after 1997 gains.

text.p: New Zealand chemicals group Fernz Corp on Wednesday reported a healthy annual profit of NZ$46.8 million ($30 million) and predicted a big jump in 1998.
The former fertiliser company has been repositioning itself as an agricultural and industrial chemicals specialist over the past 12 months, with acquisitions in Europe and Australasia.

"In 1998, the continuing operations of the company are expected to generate profit levels at least 10 percent higher than in 1997, even after absorbing higher interest and overhead costs previously applied to the fertiliser business," it said.
"This, together with the profit from the sale of the fertiliser operations, is expected to increase corporate profitability in 1998 by in excess of 50 percent," Fernz added.

Fernz sold the majority of its fertiliser making businesses in June and is currently building a French chemical connection with pharmaceuticals giant Rhone Poulenc through a planned strategic takeover of chemicals firm CFPI.
With CFPI effectively under its belt, Fernz has secured a powerful position in a niche agricultural chemicals market which analysts consider has good growth potential.

Between them Fernz and Rhone have a worldwide stranglehold on two herbicides used in conjuction with each other -- MCPA and Bromoxynil. The two companies plan to form a joint venture to market the chemicals.
Group turnover in the year increased by 30.2 percent to NZ$830.5 million. Of this 27 percent was generated in New Zealand, 48 percent in Australia and 25 percent in other international markets.

"The performance was significantly above budget and six percent ahead of last year. Part of the sales increase came from acquisition, but (French holding company) Nufarm also suceeded in extending its market share of the herbicides and the animal health products markets."
Fernz said its investment in industrial chemicals over the year had increased sales in that area of its business by 227 percent to NZ$255 million.
"In the past 12 months industrial chemicals have have risen from 12 perent to 31 percent of turnover and now represent a major sector of our international business."

For CFPI and its associated businesses, Fernz said it was difficult to make an accurate prediction for its 1998 contribution because of the restructuring planning and implementation costs still to be finalised.
"However, this business is forecast to add economic value in 1999," the company said.

Looking at other trading prospects, the company said it expected herbicide demand to remain strong internationally, trading in animal health products to expand, and profitability from chemicals trading operations to increase, partly as non-recurring costs fall away. (US$=1.53NZ$)
